- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 18d high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift unit.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+10% above 18d mean, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For horizon >14 days, model tends to underestimate true volatility; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for days 15–30 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast slope by 0.3–0.7% per sentiment unit.
